Elena — thanks for the note. I've sketched an operational acceptance plan below and attached a CSV with the step-by-step ramp (nimbus-ramp-test-plan.csv). High level acceptance criteria we propose: 

- Performance gates (must pass to move to next stage):
  * Baseline smoke: single-request latency P50 < 80ms (all paths)
  * Throughput/peak: sustained 600 requests/sec aggregate with P95 latency < 250ms and error rate < 0.5% for 10 minutes
  * Soak: 4-hour steady-state at 400 rps with no memory growth / KV cache evictions outside expected bounds
  * Failover: service fallback to smaller model variant under overload < 2x impact to 99th percentile

- Test cadence:
  1) Day 0 (smoke): connectivity, auth, minimal payloads
  2) Day 1 (baseline): 10m at expected average traffic
  3) Day 2 (peak ramp): progressive ramp to 600 rps over 30m, hold 10m, observe
  4) Day 3 (soak & regression): 4h at 400 rps, run regression prompts to verify quality metrics

- Signals we'll share: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, request traces (sampled), GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and error traces. We'll provide a Grafana board link and a CSV extract after each run.

- Ownership:
  * Redwood (camila): test harness, synthetic load driver, and Grafana dashboards
  * Nimbus (Elena/Victor): production traffic simulation, dataset for regression prompts, procurement sign-off
  * Redwood (lauren): commercial/acceptance sign-off and escalation contact

I've attached the detailed CSV plan and a canary runbook we recommend for the first canary migration. Proposed canary window: Wednesday 14 Jul 09:00-12:00 PT. Please confirm if that works for your SRE team.

Thanks — I can hop on a 30m call tomorrow to walk through the CSV.

-Markus
Markus Klein

Hi team — adding a few implementation notes from the infra side so expectations are clear before the canary: 

- Test harness: use the attached load CSV with workload buckets (read/write ratio, prompt lengths). The driver will simulate 10 user segments; default concurrency per worker = 64.
- Model variants: we'll start on gpt-m-8q (quantized) and fail over to gpt-m-8 if we observe degradation. Quantization effects on 99th percentile are expected to be +20-40ms in worst cases — will log per-model latency.
- Batching & caching: we will enable dynamic batching (max batch 128) and prefix KV cache. Please note the first-run cold-starts will show higher p95; plan your regression prompts accordingly.
- Data retention: we'll keep test traces for 30 days and provide a zipped bundle after the soak.

I've attached the canary runbook with step-by-step rollback commands and the load plan CSV I referenced earlier. During the peak ramp, we'll stream traces to the shared Grafana and Slack channel #nimbus-onboard. I'll own the load driver and will be on the call.

-Camila
Camila Reyes
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
